questions.title: GROUP BY Effect
questions.description: What does adding GROUP BY club to a query with COUNT(*) do?
questions.Option1: Sorts the rows by club
questions.Option2: Deletes duplicate rows from the table
questions.Option3: Collapses rows into groups so the count computes per group
questions.Option4: Joins the memberships table to itself

questions.title: COUNT Inside Groups
questions.description: With GROUP BY club, what does COUNT(*) mean on each output row?
questions.Option1: The number of rows in that club's group
questions.Option2: The sum of ids in the group
questions.Option3: The total row count of the table repeated on every row
questions.Option4: The number of clubs in the table

questions.title: HAVING Filters Groups
questions.description: In this snippet, what does the HAVING clause filter?
questions.Option1: Individual rows before grouping
questions.Option2: Groups after the counts are computed
questions.Option3: Columns of the result
questions.Option4: The join condition

questions.title: WHERE Filters Rows
questions.description: What does WHERE do in a grouped query?
questions.Option1: Filters groups after aggregation
questions.Option2: Filters the SELECT list
questions.Option3: Nothing — WHERE is illegal here
questions.Option4: Filters individual rows before any grouping happens

questions.title: Ungrouped Columns Rule
questions.description: In a grouped query, non-aggregated columns in the SELECT list should…
questions.Option1: Appear freely without restriction
questions.Option2: Appear in the GROUP BY list or be wrapped in an aggregate
questions.Option3: Be numeric
questions.Option4: Be aliased

questions.title: Two Group Keys
questions.description: GROUP BY club, faculty creates which granularity?
questions.Option1: One row per club
questions.Option2: One row per faculty
questions.Option3: One row per unique (club, faculty) pair
questions.Option4: One row for the whole table

questions.title: GROUPING SETS In SQLite
questions.description: What is SQLite's support for GROUPING SETS?
questions.Option1: SQLite does not support GROUPING SETS
questions.Option2: Supported with an extension
questions.Option3: Supported only with window functions
questions.Option4: It is an alias for GROUP BY

questions.title: Group Row Order
questions.description: Without ORDER BY, in what order do GROUP BY rows come back in SQLite?
questions.Option1: Insertion order
questions.Option2: Sorted by the group key
questions.Option3: Largest group first
questions.Option4: Undefined — add ORDER BY for a stable order

questions.title: HAVING Without GROUP BY
questions.description: What does HAVING mean in an aggregate query with no GROUP BY?
questions.Option1: It is a syntax error
questions.Option2: The whole table is treated as a single group
questions.Option3: It behaves exactly like WHERE
questions.Option4: It returns one row per column

questions.title: Aggregate In WHERE
questions.description: WHERE COUNT(*) > 2 (no GROUP BY trickery) — what happens in SQLite?
questions.Option1: It filters rows normally
questions.Option2: It is allowed but slow
questions.Option3: It is an error — aggregates are not allowed in WHERE
questions.Option4: It silently becomes HAVING

questions.title: Clause Pipeline Order
questions.description: Which pipeline does a grouped query follow?
questions.Option1: FROM then WHERE then GROUP BY then HAVING then SELECT then ORDER BY
questions.Option2: FROM then HAVING then WHERE then GROUP BY then SELECT then ORDER BY
questions.Option3: SELECT then WHERE then GROUP BY then HAVING then ORDER BY
questions.Option4: FROM then GROUP BY then WHERE then HAVING then ORDER BY then SELECT

questions.title: HAVING AVG Meaning
questions.description: In the snippet, what does the HAVING line do?
questions.Option1: Keeps rows whose joined_year is above 2021
questions.Option2: Keeps only clubs whose average join year exceeds 2021
questions.Option3: Sorts clubs by their average join year
questions.Option4: Errors — AVG cannot appear in HAVING

questions.title: Two Key Group Shape
questions.description: What shape does the snippet's result have?
questions.Option1: One row per club
questions.Option2: One row per faculty
questions.Option3: One row total
questions.Option4: One row per unique club-and-faculty combination
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT club, faculty, COUNT(*) FROM memberships
GROUP BY club, faculty;

questions.title: Why HAVING For Counts
questions.description: Why must COUNT(*) > 2 live in HAVING rather than WHERE?
questions.Option1: COUNT(*) works fine in WHERE too
questions.Option2: HAVING runs before rows are grouped
questions.Option3: Aggregate conditions are only legal after grouping — in HAVING
questions.Option4: HAVING is simply faster

questions.title: Where To Put The Row Filter
questions.description: active = 1 must be checked in a grouped query. Where does it belong?
questions.Option1: In HAVING — it is the newer keyword
questions.Option2: In WHERE — it filters rows before grouping (cheaper and clearer)
questions.Option3: In ORDER BY
questions.Option4: Either place, with identical semantics and cost

questions.title: GROUP BY Expression
questions.description: What does the snippet produce?
questions.Option1: One row per decade with its sign-up count
questions.Option2: One row per year
questions.Option3: An error — expressions cannot be grouped
questions.Option4: One row per member

questions.title: GROUPING SETS Theory
questions.description: In engines that support it, GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((club), (faculty)) produces what?
questions.Option1: One combined grouping of club and faculty together
questions.Option2: Only grand totals
questions.Option3: A syntax error in every engine
questions.Option4: Two row sets: totals by club alone and totals by faculty alone

questions.title: ROLLUP Theory
questions.description: In engines that support it, GROUP BY ROLLUP (a, b) aggregates at which levels?
questions.Option1: Only the (a, b) level
questions.Option2: Only the grand total
questions.Option3: Three levels: (a, b), (a), and the grand total
questions.Option4: Four levels including sub-subtotals

questions.title: Compound HAVING
questions.description: In the snippet, which clubs are listed?
questions.Option1: Clubs with two or more members, except Drama
questions.Option2: Clubs named Drama with two members
questions.Option3: All clubs
questions.Option4: An error — AND cannot combine conditions in HAVING

questions.title: WHERE And HAVING Together
questions.description: In the snippet, when does each filter run?
questions.Option1: HAVING filters rows and WHERE filters groups
questions.Option2: Both run before grouping
questions.Option3: Both run after grouping
questions.Option4: WHERE filters rows first; HAVING then filters the grouped counts
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT club, COUNT(*) FROM memberships
WHERE joined_year >= 2020
GROUP BY club
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;
